current_answer: As of 17 October 2026, public evidence does not establish broad capability decline across popular AI models. A BridgeBench result for Claude Opus 5.5 rose from 95.7% on 9 October to 105.8% on 16 October relative to its first tracked session and remains inside the publisher's 90–110% band. That counterevidence covers its private 50-task mix and composite score, not every Opus workflow. A public issue reports an October 1 behavior shift in one user's logs; the first bad day coincides with a Claude Code version change, while another commenter reports similar symptoms with an unchanged client. OpenAI closed its 13 October GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work incident at 16:36 UTC; one Windows user's issue adds later stream and remote-compaction failures on 16–17 October. These are access or request failures, not poor completed answers. Check status, preserve the original task, and compare only completed same-surface tasks with model, settings, correction cost, speed, and quota recorded.

catalogue_card.question: Did evidence catch a model getting worse—or a workflow getting harder to use?
catalogue_card.text: Opus 5.5 rose to 105.8% of its first tracked score in BridgeBench’s 16 October test, within the publisher’s band. A user report says behavior changed; one Windows Codex user still reports late failures after OpenAI closed an incident. Neither establishes broad model decline.

summary: No broad AI-model capability decline is established by this review.
BridgeBench reports Claude Opus 5.5 at 105.8% of its first tracked session on 16 October, up from 95.7% on 9 October and still within its stated 90–110% band.
An Opus 5.5 user report describes changed session-token metrics and task judgment around 1 October; the original comparison coincides with a Claude Code update and lacks a fixed-task replication.
OpenAI marked the GPT-6.1 Sol Codex/Work incident resolved on 13 October; a separate Windows user reports late stream and remote-compaction failures on 16–17 October.
A failed request and a completed poor answer are different observations. Check status and preserve work; compare same-task completions under matched settings.
uncertainty: The Opus 5.5 user issue is account-authored; its one-day post-shift sample is small, task composition is not held constant, and the client update coincides with the reported date change.

BridgeBench keeps the task prompts and tests private. Its first tracked session is the reference, and its composite includes correctness, output tokens and price; its result does not identify a model-weight change or transfer to every Claude product.
The reported Codex stream and compaction errors come from one Windows user; they do not estimate prevalence or establish a cause shared with the 13 October status incident.
No current multi-provider, matched completed-task series establishes broad model decline.
Analytics were unavailable; readership, return use, reader actions and revenue remain unknown, not zero.
freshness_note: Checked 17 October 2026. The latest Opus 5.5 benchmark result is inside its publisher-defined band; individual user reports describe a behavior concern on one Opus workflow and later request failures on one Windows Codex account. The causes and wider prevalence are unknown.
